title: Implementation Ledger Domain Model and Invariants
objective: Implement persistence-agnostic Implementation Ledger domain objects, stable enums, structured errors, value validators, and local state invariants without implementing Repository or persistence concerns.
scope: Pure frozen domain objects, enums, errors, validators, and direct relationship helpers.
Bounded domain and Context regression tests plus Context Bootstrap validation.
Domain contract, Project Memory updates, one immutable Implementation Run, and one local commit.
explicit_non_goals: No Repository interface, in-memory Repository, full graph manager, SQLAlchemy ORM, PostgreSQL table or schema, migration, session, Unit of Work, or transaction code.
No Manifest Indexer, Git consistency service, API, UI, TDX, Dataset Snapshot, Factor DSL, Optimization, Validation runtime, Registry, LightGBM, or Qlib implementation.
No Factor Lab, accepted ADR, historical Run, dependency, lockfile, runtime configuration, or secret change.
No implementation of QM2-P0-002A1b2 or later tasks.

known_limitations: No Repository, complete relationship graph cycle detection, ORM, migration, database uniqueness, concurrency control, Manifest v2, API, or UI exists.
Python 3.9 does not support dataclass slots; frozen semantics are used without slots.
Secret-like detection is conservative and is not a complete secret scanner.
Manifest v1 cannot represent arbitrary Run relationships, logical repository identity, or all domain enum vocabularies directly.
Context schema v1 cannot encode exact next task QM2-P0-002A1b2, so machine-readable task lists retain parent QM2-P0-002A1.
The containing commit cannot be embedded self-referentially; Git history resolves it after commit.
unresolved_questions: Should future Run ID uniqueness be global or repository-scoped?
Which multiple relationship combinations are valid between the same two Runs?
How should Manifest v2 represent logical repository identity and arbitrary directed Run relationships?
rollback_information: Revert the single containing commit. No database, migration, data, API, runtime, model, Qlib, UI, dependency, lockfile, configuration, accepted ADR, or Factor Lab rollback is required.
security_impact: Pure constructors conservatively reject obvious secret-like command, reason, limitation, and credential-bearing URI values without retaining rejected values; no runtime secret handling changed.
data_lineage_impact: No research data changed; the domain types prepare future implementation-lineage indexing while Git and immutable Runs remain authoritative.
